title: Fto loss converges with spliceosome perturbations through Rsrp1/Dazap1 RNA-processing markers
exact_observed_result: Fto produced only 10 FDR rows across 371818 tested rows and the densest response was in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Rsrp1 fell with logFC -0.391 and FDR 3.32e-05. In 155 MB Glut, Rsrp1 was the single BH-significant Fto row with logFC -0.605 and FDR 1.79e-09, and the restricted Fto signature correlated with Prpf6 and Ddx23 but opposed Fus.
biological_interpretation: Fto knockdown does not produce a broad m6A-regulator transcriptome at this assay layer; instead it exposes a sparse, state-restricted RNA-processing readout centered on Rsrp1 and Dazap1 and related to spliceosome perturbations in MB glutamatergic neurons.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut

exact_de_rows.cell_type: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut

caveats: All measured Fto self-test FDR values were 1.0, so Rsrp1/Dazap1 are downstream reporter candidates rather than proof of a scalar relationship to captured Fto mRNA depletion.

prior_expectation.summary: FTO is an RNA m6A demethylase with CNS functions, while RSRP1 is a spliceosome-associated arginine/serine-rich factor; the observed Fto/Rsrp1 relationship is an abundance-level bridge from m6A biology to selected splicing-factor states.
